name: Trimetazidine
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: Entered at Dr. W. Rivero's direction (Nov 17, 2026); verified against the EMA 2012 referral SmPC wording
summary: Trimetazidine is cleared mainly by the kidneys, so exposure rises as kidney function falls. Since the 2012 European Medicines Agency (EMA) review it is contraindicated in severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance [CrCl] <30 mL/min), which includes end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) and dialysis, and the dose is halved at CrCl 30–60 mL/min. It is not sold in the US, so there is no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: European summary of product characteristics (SmPC) uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault).

bands.recommendation: Usual dose: 35 mg modified-release (MR) twice daily with meals, or 20 mg immediate-release three times daily. Add-on therapy for stable angina only; reassess at 3 months and stop if no response (EMA 2012).
Moderate impairment (SmPC: CrCl 30–60): 35 mg MR once daily in the morning with breakfast, or 20 mg immediate-release twice daily. Older adults: dose by CrCl, titrate carefully (EMA 2012).

hd.text: Contraindicated (severe renal impairment, CrCl <30 mL/min; EMA 2012). Stop it in patients starting dialysis.

pd.text: Contraindicated (severe renal impairment, CrCl <30 mL/min; EMA 2012).

dialyzable: Not established; irrelevant in practice because the drug is contraindicated in kidney failure.
monitoring: Check CrCl before starting and periodically. Watch for parkinsonian symptoms, tremor, restless legs, gait instability and falls; stop trimetazidine permanently if they appear (EMA 2012). Also contraindicated in Parkinson disease and other movement disorders.

pediatric.approved_ages: Not established in patients under 18 years

sources: European Medicines Agency. (2012). Trimetazidine: Article 31 referral, Annex III (amendments to the summary of product characteristics and package leaflet). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/referrals/trimetazidine

European Medicines Agency. (2012, June 22). European Medicines Agency recommends restricting use of trimetazidine-containing medicines (EMA/CHMP/417861/2012). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/referrals/trimetazidine

revision_log.change: Created: contraindicated in advanced CKD/ESKD (CrCl <30) and dose-halved at CrCl 30–60, per Dr. Rivero's direction and EMA 2012 SmPC
